newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end up strongly, trade quiet late.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end up strongly, trade quiet late.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended higher, buoyed all session by soft May wholesale price data.
The U.S. May Producer Price Index (PPI) fell 0.3 percent both overall and excluding volatile food and energy sectors, below average forecasts for an 0.1 percent gain in both rates.
On the heels of weaker-than-expected May retail sales on Thursday, the data painted a picture of a still healthy but slowing economy, traders said.
Traders said consensus was the Federal Reserve would surely keep monetary policy unchanged at the Fed's July 1-2 policy meeting.
September Treasury bond futures climbed steadily most of the day, reaching a four-month peak at 112-02/32.
Trader turned quiet in the afternoon, with light pre-weekend profit-taking pulling some contracts from their earlier highs.
But overall, traders described the day's action as steadily bullish amid moderate interest.

"From the open we traded up, then stabilized and then slowly traded up some more to set the highs," one T-bond futures trader said. The slow but steady gains mean a knee-jerk correction from this level was less likely, he said.
He said September has built a solid base from 109-12/32 to 109-28/32 and held support at 110-12/32 on a pullback. Now 113-04/32 is the next likely upside target, he said.

December Eurodollar futures also rallied strongly for a second consecutive session, nearly challenging 94.00 resistance. But December eventually scaled back from their highs to close nearer to midrange.

"We saw minor bouts of profit-taking throughout the day," a Euro trader said. "Overall the market was pretty firm, but I think we extended our run-up just a little too much, too prematurely," he said.
Traders said Eurodollars had priced out any likelihood of an interest rate hike for the rest of the year.
"Euros may be a little ahead of themselves," the Euro trader said.
By contrast, traders in the long end said they were surprised September T-bonds stalled shy of preliminary targets of 112-4/32 to 112-8/32, especially given bond-friendly PPI.
It was the fifth straight month that producer prices declined, the first such string in 45 years.
Consumer price data will be Tuesday, and was forecast up 0.2 percent overall and excluding food and energy sectors.
"It got really quiet in the bonds late," a T-bond futures trader said. "It was another nice close, but I just notice that the market is running out of steam," he said.

At the close, September T-bonds were up 15/32 at 111-27/32, 10-yr notes rose 11/32 to 108-30/32, munis rose 10/32 to 119-18/32, Sept bills were up 0.020 point at 94.790, Dec Euros rose 0.035 to 93.965. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
